pr_title: Add parameter to limit metadata per metric in /api/v1/metadata
pr_body: Fix #10618 by adding an extra parameter called `limit-per-metric`
pr_comments:
Ok, I think it should be ready for another round of review.

I had a hard time coming up with a decent test, I ended up adding a new field, `responseMetadataTotal`, for the test struct. Which tests if the amount of returned metadata, not metric, is correct. Please let me know if you have better ideas 😬

issue_context.title: Add feature flag to control /api/v1/metadata
issue_context.body:
## Proposal

The current `/api/v1/metadata` includes every instance of the metric definition. There are [cases where application bugs introduce high cardinality HELP text](https://github.com/prometheus/jmx_exporter/issues/703).

It would be useful to have a flag to squash this and only return one (fist?) instance of the definitions in order to avoid expensive (many megabytes) of metadata being returned by this API endpoint.
comments: @roidelapluie I'm interested on working on this issue

cc @ArthurSens 

Should we instead have some API parameter for this? What it could be called? `limit-per-metric`? Might be more sensible than feature flag?

The change would be a lot simpler indeed, almost the same as suggested by @juanrh 

For adoption it would be a lot easier with a parameter too, there's no need to reconfigure the prometheus container with an extra feature flag

> Maybe `limit-help-per-metric`?

Feels a bit strange saying that we're limiting help text, but we return the whole metadata
Yea, same problem might happen for other metadata, so I think I would vote for just per metric for now, we add more granular option later on
should be ready for review now!

review_comments: We can remove new line on 1211 for readability

Maybe it's just me, but I would be more confident with slightly more unit tests. One I would like to see is a test when you have multiple `targetMetadata` values for increased [code coverage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_coverage).
I think that's a valid concern, test added :)
What if we get a negative number here?

Good point, I feel like there should be a validation for negative numbers, but since the former param `limit` also doesn't have this validation I think we should keep them consistent

Maybe we could add the validation in another PR?

The distinction is that `limit` is allowed to be 0. Below usages check `if limit >= 0` and use `-1` to represent "no limit". Maybe to keep things consistent, we should follow the same convention instead of validation?

Nice, I think to address this @ArthurSens we need to keep consistency with `limit` variable, so either (A) adding MaxInt idea to `limit` or (B) (preferably, looking by comments) bringing `limit` flow to `limitPerMetric`

For (B) it would be something like `limitPerMetric := -1` and each check `if limitPerMetric > 0 && len(ms) >= limitPerMetric {` 

The thing is that MaxInt vs -1 flow is, in this function, kind of equally complex (just in different places). However given limit already uses something, consistency would give us nice readability gains
